lessons: Review snag only; all checks passed and review again judged the seed path, lift and SeedSafety sound. Keep the design, every earlier fix and every test. Close only the foreign-intake attribution hole in `_prior_lifted`; do not redesign.

`_prior_lifted` counts any `ticket_intake` source:seed signal inside this seeder's open lift window as its own. A different seeder's intake that lands while A's window is open gets exempted, so A can overwrite B's stem. Foreign stems must always hit the collision finding.

Attribute partial lifts explicitly, never by time window. Preferred fix: have `_lift_seeds` pass the seeder to `Intake.commit` so the `ticket_intake` body carries `seeder` (a body field, not a new event type; tickets.py is fenced). Then exempt only intakes whose `seeder` equals this stem.

Replay case: a skipped already-on-main seed emits no intake. Its exemption must still come from this seeder's own attributed intake from an earlier run. Keep the run0/run1/run2 partial-lift re-offer test green.

Add a test_seeds.py or test_terminal.py case: A's lift intent opens and never completes, then seeder B lifts `b-seed`. Then A authors `tickets/b-seed/ticket.md`, and validate_batch must report `already exists on main`. Invert the assertion once to prove it can fail.

Before answering, map every AC and every earlier review finding to a named test with a real assertion: byte-binding, ordinary-run negative, no-signal admission, cap run leaves main unchanged, partial-lift re-offer, and now foreign-intake collision.
reason: Checks passed and review found only one narrow, fixable attribution defect in the partial-lift exemption; the design is judged sound.
